title: CDS market-standard quote and upfront check

items.prompt: This lesson uses MSQ as a local abbreviation for market-standard quote. Which statement matches its simplified conversion model?

options.label: MSQ is the conventional quoted spread treated as a zero-upfront par spread for calibrating the flat hazard rate
MSQ is always the fixed running coupon paid on the contract
MSQ is the signed upfront cash amount divided by notional

items.explanation: MSQ is a lesson-local label for the conventional quoted spread. The toy converter treats it as a zero-upfront par spread to infer one flat risk-neutral hazard rate; the contract can have a different fixed running coupon.

items.prompt: A simplified converter is given an MSQ of 180 basis points per year and a standard coupon of 100 basis points per year. Which rate determines the scheduled running premium cash flows?
items.explanation: The fixed standard coupon determines running premiums. The MSQ calibrates the pricing model, and the upfront amount bridges the resulting protection value and fixed-coupon premium value.

items.prompt: Calculate the signed upfront amount in USD when notional is USD 10,000,000, the quote-implied premium annuity is 4.0 model-years, MSQ is 150 basis points per year, and the fixed coupon is 100 basis points per year. Positive means paid by the protection buyer.
items.explanation: Convert the rates to 0.015 and 0.010. Then U0 = N A (sMSQ - cstd) = 10,000,000 × 4.0 × 0.005 = USD 200,000. It is positive, so the protection buyer pays it.

items.prompt: Calculate the signed upfront amount in USD when notional is USD 5,000,000, the quote-implied premium annuity is 2.5 model-years, MSQ is 300 basis points per year, and the fixed coupon is 500 basis points per year. Positive means paid by the protection buyer; enter a negative number if the buyer receives cash.
items.explanation: U0 = 5,000,000 × 2.5 × (0.03 - 0.05) = -USD 250,000. The high fixed coupon makes the running premium leg exceed protection value, so the protection buyer receives the negative signed upfront.

items.prompt: For a curve that is already calibrated and held fixed, calculate the market-standard quote in basis points per year from notional USD 8,000,000, premium annuity 4.0 model-years, fixed coupon 100 basis points per year, and signed upfront USD 160,000 paid by the protection buyer.
items.explanation: With the calibrated annuity held fixed, sMSQ = cstd + U0/(N A) = 0.01 + 160,000/(8,000,000 × 4.0) = 0.015, or 150 basis points per year. A full upfront-to-quote conversion cannot hold A fixed while the quote-implied hazard rate changes.

items.prompt: Use the lesson's one-year flat-hazard model with one annual period, zero continuously compounded risk-free rate, recovery 40%, notional USD 10,000,000, and fixed coupon 1% per year. For hazard rate lambda, A(lambda) = (1 - exp(-lambda))/lambda and the par quote is (1 - 0.40)lambda. A signed upfront of USD 195,082.302 is paid by the protection buyer. Root solve U0/N = A(lambda)[(1 - 0.40)lambda - 0.01], then report the quote in basis points per year.
items.explanation: The root is lambda = 0.05 per year: A = (1 - exp(-0.05))/0.05 = 0.97541151 and A × (0.60 × 0.05 - 0.01) = 0.0195082302, matching U0/N. The quote is 0.60 × 0.05 = 0.03, or 300 basis points per year.
